purpose: personal account of Alexey designing, implementing, and publishing SQLiteSearch

required_facts.fact: Alexey wanted a compact Python search library that was local, easy to integrate, and persistent.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 1-3: requirements and motivation are stated.

required_facts.fact: minsearch supported text and vector search with a simple API but stored its index in memory and lost data after process restart.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 3 and 15: minsearch limitations are described.

required_facts.fact: The library was needed for an AI Engineering Buildcamp project where ingestion should operate independently of the RAG agent.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 12-17: course context and independent ingestion requirement are stated.

required_facts.fact: The requirements included Python, easy local setup without Docker, and both regular text and vector search.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 21-26: all four requirements are listed.

required_facts.fact: Elasticsearch was considered too large for the small-scale use case, while Qdrant and PostgreSQL would require an external service or Docker.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 28: infrastructure trade-offs are described.

required_facts.fact: ChatGPT suggested SQLite text search, but SQLite did not provide vector search out of the box.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 36: text-search discovery and vector-search gap are stated.

required_facts.fact: lshashing, SparseLSH, and narrow-down each failed at least one requirement.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 43-49: limitations of the three options and decision to build are given.

required_facts.fact: Alexey chose locality-sensitive hashing because he understood random projections and wanted an implementation he could debug.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 55: LSH choice and debugging rationale are stated.

required_facts.fact: The project began as LightSearch and was renamed SQLiteSearch because 'litesearch' was already taken on PyPI.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 59: naming history is explicit.

required_facts.fact: Claude Code implemented the library from a plan, and the final index was stored in one SQLite file without a separate server.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 64-69 and 85-89: implementation workflow and final architecture are described.

author_attribution: Attribute the project requirements, design choices, naming, and publication workflow to Alexey; retain the intended small-project scope.
